## bdaef728db34

**Classification: reproduced shortcut plus independent lint defect.** Generator SHA-256 `8d0aadbd799594cac707e37b2d56ae31f0cdf6cbb7a677dbe838dce5caf1658b`; canonical rule hash `d518454bb493`.

The intended rule is row-local: keep the leftmost cell of every same-color horizontal run. Ordinary generation uses three to five runs and draws that many distinct colors, so every monochrome 4-connected component is itself one horizontal run. Consequently, the simpler rival **“keep one lexicographically first cell per monochrome 4-connected component”** is indistinguishable on ordinary samples.

A source-bound finite probe generated 300 ordinary grids—seeds 0–99 at sample index 0 for each of easy, medium, and hard. All 300 passed `self_check`; the rival agreed with the row-local rule on all 300. Evidence: `checks/audit/bdaef728db34/distribution.json` and `distribution-command.log`.

The exact counterexample in `checks/audit/bdaef728db34/input.json` contains a 2×2 color-2 block (two horizontal runs in adjacent rows) and one color-4 run. It passes the target validator at medium/default difficulty and conforms to the documented allowance for repeated colors and runs in different rows, but ordinary construction excludes it by assigning distinct colors. The Racket rule retains the left cell in **both** color-2 rows; the component rival retains only the top representative. They differ at row 2, column 1. Evidence: `checks/audit/bdaef728db34/racket.json` and `comparison.json`.

The focused lint stage also reproduces a missing required `RULE_HASH` and two non-probed singleton axes (`position_bias`, `density`): `checks/audit/bdaef728db34/lint-run/checks/bdaef728db34_before_lint.log`. This audit target was not edited.
